short: Parity and reflections in the Johnson walk

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.DickeSol.sDiagM_mulVec_liftSymVec
lean.annotation: Lean writes $R$ for the remaining targets and proves that the diagonal operator acts on an encoded subset $E$ by the sign $(-1)^{|E\cap R|}$. In this diagram $R=S\setminus F$. An archived target contributes a factor of $+1$. Two still-unfound targets each contribute $-1$, for a product of $+1$.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.DickeSol.u0Vec
lean.annotation: The encoding uses one increasing tuple of addresses for each subset. For $r$ remaining targets, the initial probability of $w$ hits is $\binom rw\binom{N-r}{m-w}/\binom Nm$. In particular, with two remaining targets the chance that the initial subset contains both is $m(m-1)/(N(N-1))$.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.DickeSol.johnsonSingleIter
lean.plain: One step of the Johnson walk
lean.annotation: `johnsonSingleIter` takes the reflection for the current stage as the supplied orthogonal operator $D$. The phase query is diagonal in the hit-count coordinates, and $D$ can mix them. With two remaining targets the parity signs in the three coordinates are $+1,-1,+1$. A later stage can use a different $D$.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.DickeSol.eigProj
lean.plain: Johnson eigenspace projectors from subset inclusion
lean.annotation: Johnson eigenspaces come from the subset system. The degree-zero space is the constant functions on subsets. The higher projectors are constructed from subset inclusion without using $S$, so they can act between queries even though the hit-count classes depend on $S$.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.DickeSol.rmsTagWeightKick_conj_liftSymVec
lean.plain: Phase kick by marking and uncomputing
lean.annotation: The threshold operation marks the flags, applies a sign conditioned on their count, and uncomputes the flags. The displayed identity gives the resulting phase on each subset. A block of $m$ addresses needs two marking rounds, one in each direction.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.DickeSol.symPrefixKickVec
lean.plain: Sign below or at the cutoff
lean.annotation: A phase kick changes the sign of the amplitude in every class $w\le j_0$. Each class has the same probability immediately before and after the kick. A later mixing operation can turn the change of relative signs into a change in readout probabilities.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.DickeSol.sDiagM_mulVec_liftSymVec
lean.annotation: The parity query gives phases $+1$, $-1$ and $+1$ to subsets with zero, one and two remaining hits. This diagonal operation preserves the squared amplitude of each subset. The intervening Johnson operator can mix the hit counts and change their probabilities.

statements.markdown: a sign set by the parity of how many remaining targets a set contains

lean.plain: One step of the Johnson walk
lean.annotation: `memPrefix k s` specifies which $s$ archive slots have been filled. Only those slots count when unmarking. This matters when zero is a target, because unused slots also contain zero.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.DickeSol.sDiagM_mulVec_liftSymVec
lean.annotation: The archive invariant gives $F\subseteq S$. Flipping a flag for $x\in F$ after marking cancels the mark on every archived address, giving the bit $[x\in S]\oplus[x\in F]=[x\in S\setminus F]$. With flags in $|-\rangle$, the resulting phase depends on the parity of those remaining hits.
